payload.statement: OPEN PROBLEM (source_says_open; current status unverified; result status attempted_unsolved). Prove that the phase transition of the nearest-neighbour q-state Potts model on Z^d with d >= 3 is discontinuous for every q >= 3 (equivalently q_c(d) = 2 for all d >= 3). Source: Duminil-Copin: Lectures on the Ising and Potts models on the hypercubic lattice, PIMS 2017, Conjecture 2, p. 93; also duminil_copin_icm_2018 p. 18 (q_c(d) = 2).

payload.statement: ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Examine whether the reflection-positivity chessboard argument can be pushed down from q >= q_c(d) large to q = 3 in d = 3 using improved contour entropy bounds. Result: The Kotecky-Shlosman argument proves a first-order transition when the entropy of contours (bounded by e^{c |contour|}) is beaten by the energy gain, which requires q large enough that log q exceeds a lattice-dependent constant; in d = 3 the best constants give q >= some number in the tens. Improving to q = 3 needs the exact contour entropy, which is not available; numerically the d = 3, q = 3 transition is weakly first order with a tiny latent heat, so any argument must be sharp to within a few percent, beyond what chessboard estimates give. Alternative route through the random-cluster representation: discontinuity is equivalent to non-uniqueness of the infinite-volume random-cluster measure at p_c, i.e. to the wired measure having an infinite cluster at p_c while the free one does not; for q > 4 in d = 2 this was done via the six-vertex transfer matrix, a planar tool. No d = 3 substitute. No result. Obstruction: Contour-entropy constants are far from sharp and the two-dimensional transfer-matrix route has no three-dimensional analogue.
